title: WhatGroup: test buttons clobber state, tooltip and comment drift
cluster_summary: RunTest (core/WhatGroup.lua) writes the sample into pendingInfo. That overwrites a real capture, and while the addon is stood down it leaves a withheld popup that the StandUp re-show arm displays unasked. Both problems are fixed in WhatGroup in one commit: RunTest renders the sample through the existing previewInfo/shownInfo path as a one-shot, never touches pendingInfo, and only prints the chat preview while stood down. The lifecycle test is rewritten to assert behaviour. The tooltip and comment drift (WG-R-05, WG-R-07) are cheap edits that ride along in the same file pass. No upstream route.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed in the code: RunTest sets self.pendingInfo = self:SampleInfo() and never restores it, so /wg show, the details link and launcher Show render the test group in place of the player's real capture. The preview-mode MUST does not apply, because it covers toggled preview verbs and options-ui.md:374 permits a one-shot flow. The overwrite is also documented as intended (common-tasks.md:251, data-flow.md, ARCHITECTURE.md). That makes it a UX defect, not a standards breach, and the severity drops to low.
verdicts.remediation: Same commit as WG-R-04. RunTest stops writing pendingInfo. It renders the sample through the existing previewInfo/shownInfo() path as a one-shot that is cleared on dismiss, and passes the sample to ShowNotification as an argument. No new public surface beyond what that needs. Update the test_lifecycle/test_testmode assertions. Update only the docs that describe the injection: common-tasks.md:251-253, slash-dispatch.md:89, frame.md, data-flow.md and ARCHITECTURE.md where they say RunTest injects pendingInfo, plus scope.md and module-map.md only if they say the same.

verdicts.assessment: Traced: while stood down, RunTest builds the popup with its secure teleport button and UISpecialFrames entry. visibilityAllows withholds it (gateWithheld=true), and NS.StandUp -> ApplyFrameVisibility then shows it unasked, carrying test data. The covering test checks only pendingInfo ~= nil (testing-§12). The trigger is narrow but the defect is real, and it shares its root cause with WG-R-03.
verdicts.remediation: Fold into the WG-R-03 commit. While the addon is stood down, RunTest prints the chat preview only and builds or withholds no frame. Rewrite tests/test_lifecycle.lua:485-493 to assert no frame built, pendingInfo unchanged (nil), and nothing shown after Set('enabled', true).

verdicts.assessment: Verified: the settings/Schema.lua:282 tooltip says the default is 260, but defaults/Profile.lua:40 ships 280, and the modules/Frame.lua:58-61 comment claims the shipped defaults ARE 420/260. This is drift the player can see, and a one-line fix.
verdicts.remediation: Stop restating the number in prose so it cannot drift again. Use the tooltip 'Height of the group-info popup, in pixels.' or build it from C.frame.height. Reword the Frame.lua:58-61 comment to refer to the defaults in defaults/Profile.lua and drop the 260 claim.

verdicts.assessment: Verified: the core/WhatGroup.lua:246 comment implies RunMigrations migrates the incoming profile, but RunMigrations keys off the account-wide g.schemaVersion and is a no-op once current. The core/Database.lua header already requires profile-scoped steps to walk every stored profile, so the comment misleads but has no runtime effect.
verdicts.remediation: Comment-only, done in the same pass as WG-R-03/04, not a commit of its own. Reword to: 'Idempotent; normally a no-op once the account-wide schema stamp is current. Profile-scoped steps walk every stored profile (core/Database.lua).' Keep the call. No change to Database.lua.
